newsitem.title: USA: Delta Q3 costs up on fuel price increase.
newsitem.headline: Delta Q3 costs up on fuel price increase.

text.p: Delta Air Lines Inc, the nation's third largest airline, said Thursday its third quarter operating costs increased slightly due to a 22 percent rise in fuel costs.
Third quarter operating costs per available seat mile were 8.97 cents, an increase of one percent from last year.
Excluding a fuel expense increase of 22 percent, operating costs per available seat mile declined slightly from last year. The airline did not elaborate.
Total operating expenses for the March 1997 quarter were $3.0 billion, an eight percent increase from the March 1996 quarter, the company said.

"Delta's improved unit revenues and controlled unit costs in the March quarter -- a powerful combination -- produced a remarkable financial performance for our shareowners," Ronald Allen, Delta chairman, said in a prepared statement.
For the third fiscal quarter ended March 31, Delta earned $2.47 per fully diluted share, including one-time charges, compared to a loss of $5.77 per fully diluted share last year, including charges.

During the quarter, Delta posted $52 million in charges to restructure its transatlantic routes. Last year, Delta recorded $556 million in charge to write-down costs of its Lockheed L-1011 fleet and the continuation of its cost reduction program.
Operating income for the March 1997 quarter totaled $398 million, an increase of 136 percent over the March 1996 quarter operating income of $169 million.
Third quarter operating revenue increased 15 percent to $3.4 billion from $3.0 billion last year.

Delta said the improvement in operating revenue was driven by an 11 percent increase in revenue passenger miles, a three percent improvement in the passenger mile yield, and an 84 percent increase in other revenues such as frequent flyer partnership programs, Delta's cobranded SkyMiles credit card, and code-share agreements.
Cargo revenue also increased 13 percent from the prior year.
